subject: Logic
title: Plato's Cave
description: A fast breakdown of Plato's Cave for builders.

hook.text: Prisoners chained in a cave see only shadows on the wall. They believe the shadows are all that exists.

buildup.text: Plato described this allegory around 380 BC to illustrate the difference between perception and reality.

discovery.text: One prisoner escapes and sees the sun—the source of all light. The shadows were faint copies of a fuller reality.

twist.text: When the freed prisoner returns to tell the others, they don't believe him. They prefer the familiar shadows.

climax.text: The cave asks: how much of what you believe is just the shadow of something you've never directly experienced?

punchline.text: What if your reality is someone else's shadow?

quiz.question: What does Plato's Cave allegory illustrate?
options: The gap between perception and reality
